summary: The Linux code that talks to the sound system is all in src/audio/pulse_backend.c (libpulse threaded mainloop, 3 playback streams MAIN/CUE/MONITOR plus 1 record stream). It keeps device lists that are staged and swapped in only when complete, rescans 250 ms after the last hotplug event, flushes in place with a new time base, and works out what was actually played from pa_stream_get_time. engine.c is its only caller (8 call sites plus 2 fields). The engine relies on an exact contract: lock-free SPSC rings with per-frame render tags; played_tag/consumed_frames/peak computed from write spans; ready-without-error means a transient rebuild, ready-false-with-error means loss (pause decks, loss_epoch++). Other parts of the contract: 5 s route retry, 1/2/5 s reconnect backoff, snapshots that never block (<20 ms), and flushed streams that stay ready. The spec documents this contract field by field with formulas and engine.c line references. The proposed Windows design keeps it verbatim under neutral names (radios_audio_backend_*, RadioSAudioBackendSnapshot). The design has two layers. backend_core.c is platform-neutral and holds the bus state machine, ring use, span/tag bookkeeping, refill-after-flush rule, apply/reconnect/flush decisions, atomic device-list publish and debounce. It sits on a provider vtable, with a WASAPI provider for the product and a deterministic null provider for tests. Threads: 1 manager thread (IMMDeviceEnumerator, IMMNotificationClient written in C with a refcounted relay, scans, Audiosrv status through the service manager), 3 event-driven render threads and 1 capture thread, all COM MTA and MMCSS "Pro Audio". Devices are opened asynchronously on those threads, so engine calls never block on a device except flush (bounded 100 ms handshake). Streams are shared mode, float32 stereo at the configured 44.1/48 kHz, with AUTOCONVERTPCM. Flush is Stop+Reset (clock goes to 0). Played position comes from IAudioClock::GetPosition sampled each period and is never pushed forward by the wall clock. Device ids are IMMDevice endpoint ids; "<render id>.monitor" means loopback capture. "@default" is resolved when the stream opens and never followed afterwards (same intent as Pulse DONT_MOVE). There is no fallback for explicit ids. The spec also maps every HRESULT to an operator-facing Turkish message. The old Pulse "server" argument becomes a backend selector: NULL reads RADIOS_AUDIO_SERVER, otherwise wasapi or null:<spec.json>. Virtual sinks with capture files and .monitor loopback replace pactl/parec, hotplug and server stop/start come from a watched JSON file or an in-process test API, and a manual clock gives frame-exact tests. Offline engine tests run unchanged; realtime/GUI tests run on the null provider after runner changes; test_pulse_hotplug is replaced by a fake-provider test; an opt-in WASAPI smoke test runs on the real machine.
files_touched: include/radios/output_resampler.h (internal any-rate constructor only; public behaviour unchanged)
key_decisions: Keep the backend contract identical and only rename it (radios_pulse_backend_* -> radios_audio_backend_*, RadioSPulseSnapshot -> RadioSAudioBackendSnapshot); engine.c changes are mechanical; libpulse and pulse_backend.c are removed (Windows-only product).

Split into a platform-neutral backend_core (all Pulse bookkeeping/decision logic ported verbatim) plus a provider vtable with WASAPI and null implementations; the same vtable becomes the audio I/O layer for channel_input/patchbay.

Backend-owned threads: manager (enumerator, notification client, scans, Audiosrv), 3 event-driven render threads, 1 capture thread (5 ms polling); all COM MTA, every COM object used only on its owning thread; MMCSS 'Pro Audio' on audio threads.

Shared-mode WASAPI, float32 stereo at the configured rate with AUTOCONVERTPCM|SRC_DEFAULT_QUALITY|EVENTCALLBACK|NOPERSIST; RadioS still resamples 48k->44.1k itself so snapshot.output_sample_rate proves the operator choice; fallback to the mix format with in-provider conversion and a new any-rate resampler constructor.

Flush = IAudioClient Stop+Reset on the bus thread (clock position resets to 0 = new time base), ring reset by its consumer, Pulse refill rule (480 frames / 200 ms) with Start after the first fresh write; control thread waits at most 100 ms for all buses in parallel.
played/consumed evidence = IAudioClock::GetPosition sampled every device period, clamped by written; never pushed forward by the wall clock.
output_buffer_frames reported = fill target = clamp(requested, 2*device period, buffer size); a request for 64 frames is raised to the shared-mode minimum and reported as such.

Device ids = IMMDevice::GetId endpoint strings (UTF-8); loopback inputs '<render id>.monitor' (monitor=TRUE, listed after captures); '' unassigned; '@default' = GetDefaultAudioEndpoint(eConsole) resolved when the stream opens and never followed afterwards; explicit ids never fall back.
server argument becomes a backend selector: NULL -> env RADIOS_AUDIO_SERVER -> 'wasapi'; 'null:'/'null:<spec.json>' -> null provider; anything else -> connected=FALSE with a Turkish error.

Hotplug: IMMNotificationClient callbacks only set an atomic refresh_due=now+250ms and signal the manager; only FriendlyName/DeviceDesc/DeviceFormat property changes count; default-device changes trigger a rescan only.

Connection = enumerator OK and Audiosrv RUNNING (service manager poll every 1 s, immediate on AUDCLNT_E_SERVICE_NOT_RUNNING); same 1/2/5 s backoff; device lists cleared while disconnected; 5 s route retry kept, plus an immediate retry when a configured device reappears after a rescan.

DEVICE_INVALIDATED while the endpoint is still ACTIVE (format change, sleep/resume, stall) triggers a silent reopen without an error, so the engine does not count it as a loss; a missing or removed device is reported as an error (engine pauses, as with Pulse).
Broadcast safety: per-bus named audio sessions, SetDuckingPreference(TRUE) (no communication ducking), NOPERSIST, optional RAW mode with fallback.

All backend error texts are Turkish, written as what happened + what to do, max 200 bytes, truncated only at UTF-8 boundaries; test_audio_recovery's 'fallback'/'No such' assertion changes to 'bulunamadı'.

Deterministic null provider for tests: virtual sinks on a realtime or manual clock, '<sink>.monitor' loopback, raw capture files replacing parec, hotplug and server stop/restart via a watched JSON spec or the in-process audio_null.h API; exact requested buffer size reported.
risks: IAudioClock may advance during starvation in shared mode; mitigated by min(played, written), leaving a few ms of early played_tag after an underrun.
Choosing 44.1 kHz on a 48 kHz device causes double resampling (RadioS + Windows SRC); kept on purpose to preserve the contract.
Shared-mode minimum latency is about 2 device periods (~20 ms); true low latency needs IAudioClient3 with the mix format (phase 2).
Silent reopen on invalidation differs from Pulse behaviour (loses up to one device buffer of audio); can be switched back to strict loss semantics.
WASAPI loopback sends no packets while the output is idle; needs a microphone peak decay rule; '.monitor' microphone tests are only deterministic on the null provider.

Windows default timer resolution (15.6 ms) and Windows 11 power throttling of minimised/occluded windows stretch the engine's 3 ms render poll unless the platform layer sets timeBeginPeriod(1), opts out of throttling and applies MMCSS to the engine render thread.

engine.c:1195 (and core loudness_policy.c) uses g_time_zone_new_identifier with IANA ids, which Windows GLib rejects; until the platform wrapper is used, apply_preferences fails and no device preferences are applied.
GLib monotonic clock resolution on Windows must be at most 1 ms for the refill timeouts, debounce and hotplug latency assertions (verify on GLib 2.90).
Notification callbacks can race with Unregister; handled by a refcounted relay with an alive flag.
Bluetooth Activate/Initialize can block for seconds; it runs on bus threads, so buses stay OPENING (not ready) meanwhile.
Test handle-count (fd) thresholds in the soak test need a new baseline on Windows; the null-provider capture runs in-process, unlike parec.
cross_area_dependencies: platform.h: radios_time_zone_new_identifier() must be used at engine.c:1195 (and src/core/loudness_policy.c:27-34) instead of g_time_zone_new_identifier for IANA ids.

platform.h: process-wide timer resolution (timeBeginPeriod(1)) while a realtime engine exists, plus a power-throttling opt-out (ProcessPowerThrottling with EXECUTION_SPEED|IGNORE_TIMER_RESOLUTION), and SetThreadExecutionState(ES_CONTINUOUS|ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED) while on air.
platform.h: MMCSS helper for the engine's radios-render thread (and reuse by backend threads).

channel_input.c and patchbay.c (routing/inputs area): replace their own libpulse connections with this area's provider vtable, device-id grammar (endpoint id, '.monitor', '@default') and radios_audio_server_resolve(); per-application capture needs process loopback (ActivateAudioInterfaceAsync VAD\Process_Loopback, declarations missing in mingw).
UI area: preferences.c hardware_max_rate() -> radios_audio_hardware_max_rate(); 'PulseAudio / PipeWire' label -> radios_audio_engine_backend_label(); audio_ui.c:1711 status wording.

Decoder area: test_audio transient-unload deletes a file right after unload, so the decoder must open sources with FILE_SHARE_DELETE (or close before unload returns); decoder tests use ftruncate/pwrite/open without O_BINARY.
Tools/launcher area: radios_hardware_check.py needs a 'RadioS.exe --audio-inventory-json' entry point built on this area's scan; remove libpulse from radios_launch.py/radios_package.py/radios_sdk.py.

Test-infrastructure area: run_audio_ui.py and the other runners switch from pactl/parec to null specs (RADIOS_AUDIO_SERVER=null:<json>); test-side portability for pread/fstat, /proc/self/statm, /proc/self/fd, kill/waitpid, getpid.
Build area: link ole32 uuid avrt winmm propsys mmdevapi advapi32 (psapi for tests); remove the libpulse and ALSA pkg-config checks.
platform_api_needs: GTimeZone *radios_time_zone_new_identifier(const gchar *iana_or_windows_id) — maps IANA ids to Windows zone ids (ICU) and returns NULL only for genuinely unknown zones; required at engine.c:1195.

void radios_platform_realtime_audio_begin(void) / void radios_platform_realtime_audio_end(void) — refcounted; the first begin calls timeBeginPeriod(1), opts the process out of power throttling (SetProcessInformation ProcessPowerThrottling with ControlMask EXECUTION_SPEED|IGNORE_TIMER_RESOLUTION, StateMask 0) and calls SetThreadExecutionState(ES_CONTINUOUS|ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED); the last end reverts. Called by radios_audio_engine_new/unref in realtime mode.

gpointer radios_platform_thread_audio_priority_enter(const gchar *task /* "Pro Audio" */) / void radios_platform_thread_audio_priority_leave(gpointer cookie) — AvSetMmThreadCharacteristicsW, falling back to SetThreadPriority(THREAD_PRIORITY_HIGHEST); called on the calling thread.

gboolean radios_platform_com_enter_mta(void) / void radios_platform_com_leave(gboolean entered) — CoInitializeEx(NULL, COINIT_MULTITHREADED); returns FALSE on RPC_E_CHANGED_MODE (then the caller must not CoUninitialize).
gsize radios_utf8_truncate_copy(gchar *dst, gsize size, const gchar *src) — like g_strlcpy but never cuts a UTF-8 sequence (for every 256/513-byte error/device field).

guint64 radios_platform_process_working_set(void) and guint radios_platform_process_handle_count(void) — GetProcessMemoryInfo / GetProcessHandleCount, for the soak test (replaces /proc/self/statm and /proc/self/fd).
guint32 radios_platform_process_id(void) — GetCurrentProcessId, for test device names that used getpid().
